## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables`

Create a table

Creates a managed Iceberg table from the columns in the request. Needs `CREATE_TABLE` on the namespace. Answers 404 when the environment or namespace does not exist, 409 when a table of that name exists or a deployed project declares the name (only git may take it), and 422 for an unknown column type, an empty or duplicate column name, or a namespace not rooted at `bronze`, `silver` or `gold`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

| `name` | text | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables`

List the tables of a namespace

Lists the tables of the namespace that the caller may read, with their texts in the reader's language. Needs `READ_TABLE` on the namespace; tables the caller may not read are left out. Answers 404 when the namespace does not exist, 422 for a `model_kind` no header can declare or a `lang` that is not a language tag, and 503 when the environment's storage cannot be reached (try again after `Retry-After`).

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `model_kind` | query | no | text or null | Only tables whose asset header declares this kind: fact, dimension, wide or staging. |
| `lang` | query | no | text or null | The language of the texts, such as de or fr-CH; without it, your profile's language, then Accept-Language, then the instance's main language. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | list of `TableOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}`

Show a table

Shows its texts in the reader's language, each saying which language it is in. Needs `READ_TABLE`. A view's `sql` is shown only to a reader who passes the content gate of "Defined in" (otherwise `content_reason` says why), and each shown text is recorded as `SOURCE_VIEWED`. Answers 404 when the table does not exist, 422 for a `lang` that is not a language tag, and 503 when the environment's storage cannot be reached (try again after `Retry-After`) or the audit row of a view's SQL cannot be written.

## `PATCH /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}`

Set a table's description and label

Sets the texts shown for the table in one language (`lang`, else the table's main language), or with `null` removes an edit so that the text of the project shows again. A field left out of the body stays as it is. `label_language` in the body edits the label in another language than the description, for a page that shows the two in different languages. A deploy never replaces a text set here. The table's owner or a holder of `DROP_TABLE` may do this, and must be able to read the table. Answers 404 when the table does not exist and 422 for a body with neither field, a blank text, a description over 4,000 characters, a label over 100 characters or on several lines, a `lang` or `label_language` that is not a language tag, or a `label_language` without a `label`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `lang` | query | no | text or null | The language edited, such as fr; without it, the table's main language. The answer's texts are in it too. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `DescriptionIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text or null | no |  |

| `label_language` | text or null | no |  |

## `DELETE /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}`

Drop a table

From the web interface a drop needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token never does. This holds with or without `purge`; undrop asks for no touch.

Removes the table from the catalog at once, with its grants, row filters and column masks. Needs `DROP_TABLE`. A managed table keeps its files for the undo period (7 days unless the operator changed it), during which it can be restored, and then they are deleted; an external table's files and a view are never deleted. With `purge` set, the files are due at once, the next clean-up deletes them and the table cannot be restored. Answers 404 when the table does not exist, and 409 when a deployed project builds the table or view: what git defines is changed in git, so remove the asset there and deploy, then drop it from Orphans. The message names the file to a caller who may read the table. Neither `purge` nor break-glass gets past this.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `purge` | query | no | true or false | `true` makes the files due at once: the next sweep deletes them, and the table cannot be restored. |
| `break_glass_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why the protection of a protected environment is broken, up to 500 characters; recorded in the audit log. Only a protected environment needs it. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/health`

Show a table's health

Shows the table's last maintenance, the newest result of each of its checks, its health signals and, when asked, who read it. Needs `READ_TABLE`. Answers 404 when the table does not exist and 422 when `days` is outside 1 to the period the server keeps. Answers 503 when `readers` names someone other than the caller and the audit entry for that could not be written; nothing is returned then.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `days` | query | no | whole number or null | The window of the readers in days, from 1 to the kept period (`LAKANA_TABLE_READS__KEEP_DAYS`, 90 by default); the default window (`LAKANA_TABLE_READS__DEFAULT_DAYS`, 30) when absent. |
| `readers` | query | no | true or false | False leaves the readers out of the answer; it then looks up no names and writes no `ACTIVITY_VIEWED` audit entry. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `TableHealthOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `TableHealthOut`

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/health/signals`

List the history of a table's health signals, newest first

Needs `READ_TABLE`. The values of a masked column, and every null rate and range under a row filter that applies to the caller, are left out. Answers 404 when the table does not exist and 422 for `days` outside 1 to the kept period, an unknown `signal` or a foreign `cursor`.

| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |

| `signal` | query | no | text or null | Only this signal. |
| `column` | query | no | text or null | Only this column. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | The most rows of the page (1 to 200, default 100). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |

## `PUT /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/columns/{column}/description`

Set a column's description and label

Works as the table's route does, for one column, which must be in the table's schema: the texts are set in `lang`, else in the table's main language, the label in `label_language` when the body names one, `null` removes an edit, and a field left out stays. The caller owns the table or holds `DROP_TABLE` on it, and may read it. Answers 404 for a missing table or column and 422 as the table's route does.

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/lineage`

Show a table's lineage

Walks the recorded lineage of the table: the tables it was derived from and the tables derived from it. A table or artifact written by a Python asset that declares connections also lists each connection as a source (`kind` ``CONNECTION``), shown only to a caller who may read the environment's connections. Needs `READ_TABLE` on the table itself. Answers 404 when the table does not exist.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `direction` | query | no | one of `upstream`, `downstream` | `upstream` (the default) or `downstream`. |
| `depth` | query | no | whole number | Hops to walk, 1 to 10 (default 3). |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `LineageOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `LineageOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root_id` | text | yes |  |
| `direction` | text | yes |  |
| `depth` | whole number | yes |  |
| `nodes` | list of `LineageNodeOut` | yes |  |
| `edges` | list of `LineageEdgeOut` | yes |  |
| `hidden_nodes` | whole number | yes |  |
| `truncated` | true or false | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/maintenance`

Queue maintenance for a table

Queues expiring the table's old snapshots and deleting its orphaned files, and answers 202 with a query id to poll. A worker does the work; the finished status carries a `maintenance.report` whose `note` says why part of the run was skipped, if it was. Needs `MAINTAIN_TABLE` on the table and `SUBMIT_QUERY` on the environment. Answers 404 when the table does not exist.

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/preview`

Queue a preview of a table or view: its first 100 rows, read as you

Queues your own query of `SELECT * … LIMIT 100`, written by the server, and answers 202 like the query submit route; poll its status, then fetch the rows with `…/queries/{query_id}/result?format=json`. The request takes no body and no parameter: the server builds the SQL and the limit. The query reads with your own row filters and column masks, and the result names the masked columns. Needs `READ_TABLE` on the table, then `SUBMIT_QUERY` on the environment (a Viewer is refused and told to ask for the Analyst role); a task cannot preview. Answers 403 alike for a table you may not read and one that does not exist, 404 when the environment does not exist or for a table you may read that is gone, and 409 for an artifact (download it instead) and for a namespace or table name with a dot, which a query cannot name yet.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table or view name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | Successful Response | `QuerySubmitOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `QuerySubmitOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_id` | text | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/definition`

Tell where the environment's current deployment defines a table

Answers the repository, the file's path and line, the deployed commit and project version, and an HTTPS link to the line on the git host when the repository is on one of the five public hosts. The commit is always the one deployed, never the branch head. The request takes no parameter beyond the table's name: the server finds the file from the current deployment, so no path, commit or version is ever read from the caller. Needs `READ_TABLE` on the table; a reader of the table sees the repository's name and link without any right on the environment. A table no current deployment defines answers 200 with `defined: false` and every other field `null`. Answers 403 alike for a table you may not read and one that does not exist, and 404 when the environment does not exist or for a table you may read that is gone.

| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |

| `name` | path | yes | text | Table or view name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `TableDefinitionOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `TableDefinitionOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defined` | true or false | yes |  |
| `repository` | text or null | yes |  |
| `path` | text or null | yes |  |
| `commit` | text or null | yes |  |
| `line` | whole number or null | yes |  |
| `project_version_id` | text or null | yes |  |
| `deployed_at` | text (date-time) or null | yes |  |
| `browse_url` | text or null | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/definition/file`

Give the file that defines a table, when you may see its text

Answers the location as `…/definition` does, with the file's text read from what Lakana recorded at deploy, never from the repository or the git host. The text is shown only to someone who may read the environment (`READ_ENVIRONMENT`) and every table the file uses, the table itself included, with no row filter or column mask applying to them on any of those tables, when no other table the file uses is a view, and when the file reads no file path and uses no connection. Anyone else gets `content: null` with `reason: restricted` and one sentence that names no table and no failed condition. `not_recorded` means the deployed version has no record of the file (deploy a new commit), and `too_large` a file over 1 MiB. Each read of a text is recorded in the audit log as `SOURCE_VIEWED`, once per reader, table and commit within `LAKANA_VIEW_AUDIT__WINDOW_MINUTES`, before the text is returned. Needs `READ_TABLE` on the table. Answers 403 alike for a table you may not read and one that does not exist, 404 when the environment does not exist or for a table you may read that is gone, and 503 with `Retry-After` when the audit row could not be written; no text is returned then.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table or view name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `TableDefinitionFileOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `TableDefinitionFileOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defined` | true or false | yes |  |
| `repository` | text or null | yes |  |
| `path` | text or null | yes |  |
| `commit` | text or null | yes |  |
| `line` | whole number or null | yes |  |
| `project_version_id` | text or null | yes |  |
| `deployed_at` | text (date-time) or null | yes |  |
| `browse_url` | text or null | yes |  |
| `content` | text or null | yes |  |
| `bytes` | whole number or null | yes |  |
| `reason` | one of `restricted`, `not_recorded`, `too_large` or null | yes |  |
| `message` | text or null | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/rebuild`

Rebuild a table a deployed project builds: drop it and queue a run of its asset

For a table that has to be built again from scratch from git. In one transaction it drops the table, which stays restorable with undrop for the undo period like any drop, and queues a run of exactly the asset that declares it; the answer names that run. Needs `DROP_TABLE` on the table and `RUN` on the environment. From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token never does. In a protected environment it needs `?break_glass_reason=`, and the deployment's run principal writes the table. The repository's file is named only to a caller who may read the table (`path` is `null` otherwise). Answers 404 when the table does not exist, 409 when it is an artifact, when no deployed project declares it (drop it instead), when another run of the project is active (nothing is dropped; wait for it and rebuild again) or when a protected environment has no run principal, and 422 when the reason is not 10 to 500 characters on one line.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `break_glass_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why the protection of a protected environment is broken, up to 500 characters; recorded in the audit log. Only a protected environment needs it. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `TableRebuildIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | text | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | Successful Response | `TableRebuildOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `TableRebuildOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | text | yes |  |
| `run_id` | text | yes |  |
| `repository` | text | yes |  |
| `path` | text or null | yes |  |

## `PUT /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/retention`

Set a table's retention

Sets when a managed table expires: `days` after its last activity, `on` a given day, or `never`. The table's owner may always. Anyone else needs `DROP_TABLE` for a setting that makes the table expire earlier than now, or at all, and `WRITE_TABLE` to make it expire later or never; a refusal is audited. Answers 404 when the table does not exist and 422 unless exactly one valid rule is given, the table is managed, and, for `days` or `on`, the environment is not protected.

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/data`

Append rows to a table

A run of a deployed asset may send its record of the files it read as the schema metadata `lakana.files_read`; it is recorded with the commit, and a malformed one, or one from any other caller, is a 422.

Adds the rows of an Arrow IPC stream, sent as the request body, to a managed table. Each `source` (repeatable) names a table the rows were derived from; it must exist and be readable by the caller, and records a lineage edge. Needs `WRITE_TABLE` on the table. Answers 404 when the table or a source does not exist, 409 when `expected_snapshot_id` no longer matches, 413 for a body over the server's limit, 408 when the body arrives too slowly and 503 when the server is busy with other uploads (try again after `Retry-After`).

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `source` | query | no | list of text or null | Dotted names of the tables the rows came from. |
| `source_version` | query | no | list of text or null | ``&lt;version&gt;:&lt;dotted name&gt;`` for each source that is an artifact, when the task read a specific version; the edge records it instead of the current one. A malformed value is a 422 before the body is read. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | query | no | text or null | The table's current snapshot as the caller read it, or `none`; the write commits only while that still holds (409 otherwise). |
| `break_glass_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why the protection of a protected environment is broken, up to 500 characters; recorded in the audit log. Only a protected environment needs it. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `AppendOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `408` | No part of the request body arrived within the read timeout. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `AppendOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rows` | whole number | yes |  |
| `files` | whole number | yes |  |
| `snapshot_id` | whole number or null | yes |  |

Replace all rows of a table

A run of a deployed asset may send its record of the files it read as the schema metadata `lakana.files_read`; it is recorded with the commit, and a malformed one, or one from any other caller, is a 422.

Replaces every row of a managed table with the rows of an Arrow IPC stream, sent as the request body, in one snapshot; the table keeps its history. Takes the same `source` and `expected_snapshot_id` as the append. Needs `WRITE_TABLE` on the table, and `CREATE_TABLE` as well to create a missing table with `expected_snapshot_id=none`. Answers 404 when the table or a source does not exist, 409 when `expected_snapshot_id` no longer matches, 413 for a body over the server's limit, 408 when the body arrives too slowly, 503 when the server is busy with other uploads (try again after `Retry-After`) and 422 when the upload does not fit the table (the message shows the difference).

| `expected_snapshot_id` | query | no | text or null | The table's current snapshot as the caller read it, or `none`; the write commits only while that still holds (409 otherwise). On replace, `none` also creates a missing table from the upload. |
| `break_glass_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why the protection of a protected environment is broken, up to 500 characters; recorded in the audit log. Only a protected environment needs it. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/merge`

Merge rows into a table on a key

A run of a deployed asset may send its record of the files it read as the schema metadata `lakana.files_read`; it is recorded with the commit, and a malformed one, or one from any other caller, is a 422.

Sends the rows of an Arrow IPC stream as the request body. A row whose `key` (repeatable, required: one or more columns) matches a row of the table replaces it; any other row is inserted; nothing is deleted. One snapshot: readers see the table before or after, never a half. Takes the same `source`, `source_version` and `expected_snapshot_id` as the append, and the same body limits. Needs `WRITE_TABLE` and `READ_TABLE` on the table (a merge compares the rows with the table's), and `CREATE_TABLE` as well to create a missing table with `expected_snapshot_id=none`; it is refused (422) while a row filter or column mask on the table applies to the caller. Answers 404 when the table or a source does not exist, 409 when `expected_snapshot_id` no longer matches, 413 for a body over the server's limit, 408 when the body arrives too slowly, 503 when the server is busy with other uploads (try again after `Retry-After`) and 422 for a key column the table or the rows do not have, a null key, a key that repeats in the rows or matches two rows of the table (counts only, never values), a key of several columns with more than 5,000 rows, or rows that do not fit the table.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `source` | query | no | list of text or null | Dotted names of the tables the rows came from. |
| `source_version` | query | no | list of text or null | ``&lt;version&gt;:&lt;dotted name&gt;`` for each source that is an artifact, when the task read a specific version; the edge records it instead of the current one. A malformed value is a 422 before the body is read. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | query | no | text or null | The table's current snapshot as the caller read it, or `none`; the merge commits only while that still holds (409 otherwise). `none` also creates a missing table from the rows. |
| `key` | query | yes | list of text | The columns that identify a row; repeat the parameter for a key of several columns. |
| `break_glass_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why the protection of a protected environment is broken, up to 500 characters; recorded in the audit log. Only a protected environment needs it. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `MergeOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `408` | No part of the request body arrived within the read timeout. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `MergeOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_id` | whole number or null | yes |  |
| `rows_inserted` | whole number | yes |  |
| `rows_updated` | whole number | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/history`

Keep the versions of a dimension's rows: open, close and leave alone, in one snapshot

Sends the current state of every row as an Arrow IPC stream. Against the table's open versions, a new key opens a version, a key whose values changed closes its version and opens a new one, an unchanged key is left alone, and with `close_missing=true` a key the rows lack is closed. Nothing is deleted. A key's first version always starts at 0001-01-01 UTC, so that every row of a fact finds it; `valid_from` and the run's start time date later versions. A Python asset with `write="history"` calls this; there is no CLI command. Takes the same `source`, `source_version` and `expected_snapshot_id` as the merge, and the same body limits. Needs `WRITE_TABLE` and `READ_TABLE` (and `CREATE_TABLE` to create the table with `expected_snapshot_id=none`); refused (422) while a row filter or column mask on the table applies to the caller. Answers 404 when the table or a source does not exist, 409 when `expected_snapshot_id` no longer matches or another writer committed first, 413/408/503 as the merge, and 422 for what the history write refuses (counts, never values), including more open versions than `LAKANA_RUN__MAX_HISTORY_OPEN_VERSIONS` allows.

An upload that carries a record of files read (the schema metadata `lakana.files_read`) is a 422: only an append, a replace or a merge records one.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `key` | query | yes | list of text | The natural key's columns; repeat the parameter for a key of several columns. |
| `valid_from` | query | no | text or null | The column each later version's start is read from; without it, the time the run began (or the server's time for a call outside a run). A key's first version always starts at 0001-01-01 UTC. |
| `source` | query | no | list of text or null | Dotted names of the tables the rows came from. |
| `source_version` | query | no | list of text or null | ``&lt;version&gt;:&lt;dotted name&gt;`` for each source that is an artifact. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | query | no | text or null | The table's current snapshot as the caller read it, or `none`, which also creates a missing table. |
| `close_missing` | query | no | true or false | Close the open version of each key the rows lack. |
| `break_glass_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why the protection of a protected environment is broken, up to 500 characters; recorded in the audit log. Only a protected environment needs it. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `HistoryOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `408` | No part of the request body arrived within the read timeout. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `HistoryOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_id` | whole number or null | yes |  |
| `versions_opened` | whole number | yes |  |
| `versions_closed` | whole number | yes |  |
| `closed_missing` | whole number | yes |  |
| `created` | true or false | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/namespaces/{path}/tables/{name}/load`

Load rows into a table of the bronze layer

The route `lakana load` calls: it writes the rows of an Arrow IPC stream, sent as the request body, into a table whose first namespace segment is `bronze`, and refuses any other target with 422 before it reads the body, for every client alike. `expected_snapshot_id=none` creates a missing table (`CREATE_TABLE` as well as `WRITE_TABLE`); otherwise `write` replaces or appends (`WRITE_TABLE`), committing only while the table's snapshot is still `expected_snapshot_id`. `dry_run=true` runs every check, the schema of the (usually empty) stream against an existing table included, and writes nothing. In a protected environment a load, its dry run included, needs `break_glass_reason` and `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT` (403 before the body otherwise). Answers 404 when the namespace does not exist (naming the command that creates it) or the table does not and no pin was sent (naming `none`), 409 when the snapshot moved, 413 for a body over the server's limit, 408 when it arrives too slowly and 503 when the server is busy with other uploads.

An upload that carries a record of files read (the schema metadata `lakana.files_read`) is a 422: only an append, a replace or a merge records one.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `path` | path | yes | text | Dot-joined namespace path; its first segment must be `bronze`. |
| `name` | path | yes | text | Table name. |
| `write` | query | no | one of `replace`, `append` | ``replace`` (the default) or ``append``; a first load creates the table either way. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | query | no | text or null | The table's current snapshot as the caller read it, or `none` for a missing table. |
| `dry_run` | query | no | true or false | Check only; write nothing. |
| `break_glass_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why the protection of a protected environment is broken, up to 500 characters; recorded in the audit log. Only a protected environment needs it. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `LoadOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `408` | No part of the request body arrived within the read timeout. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `LoadOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_id` | whole number or null | yes |  |
| `rows` | whole number | yes |  |
| `created` | true or false | yes |  |
| `dry_run` | true or false | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/dropped-tables`

List the dropped tables of an environment

Lists the tables dropped from any namespace of the environment whose files are not deleted yet, newest drop first. Needs `READ_ENVIRONMENT`; a table the caller may not read is left out. Answers 404 when the environment does not exist and 422 when the cursor is not one this list issued.

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |

| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most tables returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `next_cursor` | text or null | no |  |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/expiring-tables`

List the tables about to expire

Lists the managed tables of the environment that expire within `within_days`, soonest first. Needs `READ_ENVIRONMENT`. Answers 404 when the environment does not exist and 422 when `within_days` is out of range or the cursor is not one this list issued. The cursor of the next page is in the `X-Next-Cursor` response header and is absent on the last page.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `within_days` | query | no | whole number or null | The window, 1 to 3,650 days; the server's warning window (7 days by default), or 1 when that is 0, when absent. |
| `namespace` | query | no | text or null | Only the tables of this dot-joined namespace and of the ones beneath it. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most tables returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `X-Next-Cursor` of the previous page; send the same `within_days` and `namespace`. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | list of `TableRetentionOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |
